records.name: SAS Date Value (Days since 1960-01-01)

interpretation.description: Number of days before or after January 1, 1960. 0 corresponds to 1960-01-01. Negative numbers represent dates prior to 1960.
interpretation.missing_value_representation: Represented by SAS numeric missing values (. or .A-.Z), which evaluate as less than all valid numbers.

ambiguity.reason: Standard SAS date convention. Ambiguity arises only if mistaken for SAS datetime (which uses seconds) or Unix epoch.

validation_rules: Integer day value (fractional parts are truncated by SAS date formats)
Must verify value is not a SAS missing value before arithmetic

records.name: SAS Datetime Value (Seconds since 1960-01-01 00:00:00)

interpretation.description: Number of seconds since midnight on January 1, 1960. One day equals 86,400 seconds.
interpretation.conversion_to_sas_date: DATEPART(sas_datetime) extracts day count; multiplying sas_date by 86400 produces sas_datetime at midnight.

validation_rules: Do NOT add integer days directly: adding 1 increments by 1 second, not 1 day

records.name: POSIX / Unix Timestamp (Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC)

interpretation.description: Standard POSIX epoch timestamp. Offset between Unix Epoch (1970-01-01) and SAS Epoch (1960-01-01) is exactly 315,619,200 seconds (3653 days).

validation_rules: 315619200 seconds offset between SAS and Unix epoch (or 3653 days)

records.name: Excel Serial Date (1900 Date System)

interpretation.description: Days since 1900-01-01, but Excel incorrectly treats 1900 as a leap year (Lotus 1-2-3 compatibility bug). Effective epoch for post-1900-02-28 dates is 1899-12-30.

ambiguity.reason: 1900 leap year bug causes off-by-one error for dates prior to March 1, 1900.

validation_rules: Subtract 1 day if converting pre-1900-03-01 date in 1900 date system
